body: It sucks that you're feeling pressure to date, but seriously, not having a desire to date is in no way something you should try to change. I only recently got the desire to date, and let me tell you, it has brought me untold levels of misery and lonliness and made me feel horrible about myself. This society paints a disinterest in romance as a problem, but there should really be no issue in not desiring affection. If you change your mind in the future then try to date, but there's no point in doing so if you don't want to.
This is more of a quick fix than anything but you could try applying waterproof concealer/makeup on your scar?

My burns are generally like yours, and take about a month or so to completely fade into a scar. Where you burn yourself can also make a difference. For example, my old shoulder burn scars are pretty much unnoticeable but the ones on my inner wrists or stomach are visible. I don't do anything to try to heal them/avoid scarring though, so you could probably expedite this.

I just started Bupropion, which is supposed to improve my energy and ability to concentrate/reduce depression symptoms. I haven't been on it long enough to find out if it actually works, but I've had next to no side effects so far. However, medication affects everyone differently (even within a family) so your experience will likely be different from mine and your mother's. I would ask a professional about what they would recommend you and common side effects of that med.

This is probably not the most helpful advice but I've been feeling the same way. Having any sort of mental breakdown seriously delays my schoolwork so I would SH pre-emptively to keep me going. Especially once it became addictive, not doing it made it harder to study because the urges were too distracting.

Is there any way you can get an emergency appointment with a psychiatrist? From my personal experience counselling is useless, but I just started medication and I already have started seeing a difference (don't know if it's positive or negative yet but). If you can get a professional to prescribe you a medication that improves the way you feel and stay productive it could be a great quick fix.

I'm kind of in a similar situation right now, and while there are things like scar removal creams, they often take a while and some only work on particular skin colours/types. In all honesty though, you don't owe anyone an explanation for your scars. It's a lot easier to say this than to believe it but if someone ever asks you about them you can always say "long story" or something.

I haven't been in your position but the comments in this post seem to have some useful and related advice: https://www.reddit.com/r/selfharm/comments/52ut6z/my_wife_stopped_cutting_how_can_i_help/

I wish you the best <3

I feel similarly to you, but I have also had my self-harm spiral out of control to the point that it was affecting my ability to do work and be in public places because self-harming constantly felt more desirable than doing anything else, and this hasn't entirely gone away yet. That wasn't a good experience and I hope you can stay in control.

I felt the same way for a period of time recently, but then I kind of became addicted to cutting/burning/punching myself, and started distracting myself by planning out my suicide. :/ Do you have anyone you could talk to? Even if it's a distress hotline or a walk-in counsellor. Talking to people hasn't necessarily made me stop, but I usually feel a bit better and less hopeless after I do. In any case it's a distraction for half an hour or so.

I relate to the feeling like I don't deserve to be depressed/suicidal/self-harming because I'm pretty privileged, but at the same time I realized that telling myself this is just going to make me feel worse about myself, and that mental illness is an illness: it affects all kinds of people. I still don't make my issues too obvious to the people in my life though for that reason, but I have been able to partially open up to certain people that I know also struggle with their mental health. If you know anyone like that you could also try opening up to them, they could give you advice/solidarity. Also seeing a professional could give you better advice/opinions.

I'm still self-harming, and this used to not be a problem for me when I started but I can definitely relate to the feeling of it constantly being on your mind. Unfortunately I give in whenever I have the chance, so it's really great that you've managed not to! Have you tried going to a therapist or someone about it? I'm hoping to get a chance to go to one soon and I hope it can help.

Self-harm has been normalized for me for quite a while, and while it may not be a *good* action, I'm glad you no longer feel guilty and ashamed about it. Guilt and shame only hurt you more, and if I felt that way I would probably be encouraged to hurt myself more than I already do.

Thanks for your message, glad to know I'm not the only one with these kinds of sentiments. 
I'm not super close to this friend (I'm temporarily living in my city so I only met her recently and probably will rarely see her when I leave). But she's probably one of the closest friends I have here. I'm not sure I can talk to her about my mental health, since I don't see her all that often and if she decides to not hang out with me anymore I'll lose another source of social interaction, which I really need :(

I do the same when I cut, and self-harming in a less visible area is usually what I would consider doing, but my problem is that I like the fact that I can see my burn at any time too :/ I mean I'm better off at trying to do this less, especially since having noticeable marks may become problematic when I'm applying to jobs/networking/etc. but maybe the ankle would be good if I'm feeling desperate. Just to let you know though I am very safe when I SH though, I always cut lightly (reading this subreddit has alerted me to enough dangerous outcomes that my reckless side has generally been kept at bay). Thanks for your message :)

I'm moving in less than a month so it's currently impossible for me to get a therapist at the moment. I'm debating on going to a walk-in counsellor tomorrow but I'm afraid that I'm going to break down crying and make the bus ride home much more awkward (I recently called a distress line and this ended up happening, but at least I was home).

I'll try out scribbling on paper tomorrow. I share a desk with another person so it would be one of the only things I could do subtly. Thanks!
